does: Sprinkles a thin, even layer of sugar over a cold, set custard and melts it with strong heat from above until it turns into a thin, glassy, amber crust that cracks under a spoon, while the custard beneath stays cold. The Catalan word for it is cremar, to burn.
how: Have the custard cold and firm, with a dry surface. Get the torch lit or the grill very hot before the sugar goes on.
Scatter an even, thin layer of sugar over the surface, tilting the dish so that it reaches every corner, and tip off the extra.
Pass the flame slowly just above the sugar, or slide the dish close under a very hot grill, until the sugar melts and turns amber. Keep it moving so that it browns evenly and does not scorch.
Leave it a moment to harden into a glassy crust, and serve soon after.

cues.text: The sugar melts to a clear syrup and darkens evenly to deep amber, with no black patch.
The hardened crust cracks with a light tap of a spoon.
Toasted and bittersweet. A sharp, acrid smell means it has burnt.

mistakes.mistake: Using a thick layer of sugar, so that the crust is hard and gritty in places and still sugar in others.
mistakes.fix: Scatter a thin layer and tip off the extra.

mistakes.mistake: Holding the flame still, which scorches one spot and leaves the rest pale.
mistakes.fix: Keep the flame moving in slow passes over the whole surface.

mistakes.mistake: Burning a warm custard, which softens and melts the crust.
mistakes.fix: Chill the custard until it is cold and firm first.

mistakes.mistake: Burning the sugar long before serving, so that the crust draws moisture and goes soft.
mistakes.fix: Burn it just before the dish goes to the table.

comes_after.why: The custard has to be cold and firm before the sugar goes on, or the crust melts into it.
A cook who knows how sugar melts and darkens can judge the colour of the crust.

variant_of.differs: The sugar is scattered dry in a thin layer over a cold custard and burned in place in moments by heat from above, so that it sets as a crust on the dish. A caramel is cooked in a pan to a syrup that is used apart.
The top that browns is sugar, not cheese or sauce, and it is burned for moments only so that the cold custard beneath stays cold. A gratin is browned on a hot dish that is eaten warm.
